t.6.116.1: Placing his joined palms upon his head, Bharata, who increased the joy of Kaikeyī, spoke to Rāma, his elder brother, whose valour was true.
t.6.116.2: My mother has been honoured, and this kingdom was given to me. That I now give back to you, just as you gave it to me.
t.6.116.3: Like a young calf, I am not able to bear the heavy burden, the yoke laid down by a mighty bull that carried it alone.
t.6.116.4: Like a dam breached by a mighty rush of water and leaking away, this breach in the kingdom, left unclosed, I deem hard to repair.
t.6.116.5: As a donkey cannot match the gait of a horse, or a crow that of a swan, so I am unable to follow your path, O lord, O subduer of foes.
t.6.116.6: And just as a tree planted within the inner courtyard of a dwelling grows up mighty and very hard to climb, with a massive trunk and spreading branches,
t.6.116.7: Having blossomed, it would wither away and show no fruit; it would not fulfill the purpose of the one for whose sake it was planted.
t.6.116.8: This is the simile, O mighty-armed one, and you should grasp its meaning, if you, O lord of men, do not rule over us, your devoted servants.
t.6.116.9: Let the world on every side behold you today, consecrated, blazing with brilliant splendor like the scorching sun at midday.
t.6.116.10: To the resounding of massed instruments, to the jingling of girdles and anklets, and to the sound of sweet songs, may you awaken and may you sleep.
t.6.116.11: As long as the wheel turns and as far as the earth extends, so long may you here exercise lordship over all.
t.6.116.12: Having heard Bharata's words, Rāma, the conqueror of enemy cities, accepted them, saying "So be it," and sat down upon the splendid seat.
t.6.116.13: Then, at Śatrughna's command, skilled barbers, gentle of hand and very quick, attended upon Rāghava.
t.6.116.14: But first, when Bharata had bathed, and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa too, and Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, and Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas,
t.6.116.15: His matted locks cleansed, bathed, adorned with bright garlands and fragrant unguents, and clad in costly garments, he stood there, blazing with splendor.
t.6.116.16: The valiant and splendid one, who increases the glory of the Ikṣvāku line, had the grooming and adornment of Rāma and of Lakṣmaṇa carried out.
t.6.116.17: And then all the wives of Daśaratha, those noble-minded women, adorned Sītā themselves with their own hands, making her look enchanting.
t.6.116.19: Then, at Śatrughna's command, the charioteer named Sumantra yoked a chariot beautiful in every part and drove it forward.
t.6.116.18: Then Kausalyā, overjoyed and full of love for her son, carefully adorned all the wives of the Rāghavas.
t.6.116.20: Seeing the divine chariot standing ready, resembling the disc of the sun, the mighty-armed Rāma, whose valour was true, mounted it.
t.6.116.21: But in Ayodhyā, the ministers who had served King Daśaratha, placing the family priest at their head, took counsel together on what was fitting.
t.6.116.22: They took counsel for Rāma's prosperity and for the welfare of the city: "You should carry out everything for the consecration of the great-souled Rāma, who is worthy of victory, whatever is to be done with auspicious rites."
t.6.116.23: Having thus instructed the family priest, all those ministers swiftly went out from the city, their minds set on seeing Rāma.
t.6.116.24: Like thousand-eyed Indra on his chariot yoked with bay horses, the sinless Rāma mounted his chariot and set out for the finest of cities.
t.6.116.25: Bharata took hold of the reins, Śatrughna took up the parasol, and Lakṣmaṇa fanned him over his head with a fan.
t.6.116.26: Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, held a white whisk of yak-tail hair, and Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, held another, shining like the moon.
t.6.116.28: Then Sugrīva, the greatly radiant lord of the monkeys, mounted the elephant named Śatruṃjaya, which was like a mountain.
t.6.116.27: In that sky, as Rāma was being praised by the hosts of sages and by the gods together with the bands of Maruts, a sweet sound was heard.
t.6.116.29: The monkeys, having assumed human form and adorned with every ornament, went forth mounted on nine thousand elephants.
t.6.116.30: Amid the resounding blasts of conch-shells and the booming of kettledrums, the tiger among men proceeded to that city garlanded with mansions.
t.6.116.31: Then they beheld Rāghava, the matchless chariot-warrior, approaching on his chariot together with those who went before him, shining resplendent in his form.
t.6.116.32: Having hailed Kākutstha and been greeted in return by Rāma, they followed the great-souled one, who was surrounded by his brothers.
t.6.116.33: Surrounded by his ministers, by brāhmaṇas, and likewise by the people of the realm, Rāma shone with splendor like the moon amid the stars.
t.6.116.34: He went forth surrounded by joyful people who walked ahead of him with musical instruments, holding cymbals and svastikas in their hands and proclaiming auspicious blessings.
t.6.116.35: Cows, maidens and twice-born men, along with men holding sweetmeats in their hands, went on ahead of Rāma, bearing unbroken grains of rice and gold.
t.6.116.36: Then Rāma told the ministers of his friendship with Sugrīva, of the might of the son of the Wind, and of that deed of the monkeys. Hearing it, the dwellers of the city of Ayodhyā were filled with wonder.
t.6.116.37: Having spoken thus, the radiant Rāma, surrounded by the monkeys, entered Ayodhyā, which was thronged with joyful and well-nourished people.
t.6.116.38: Then the citizens raised banners on every house, and he reached his father's lovely palace, once inhabited by the descendants of Ikṣvāku.
t.6.116.39: Having reached the palace of his great-souled father and entered it, he respectfully saluted Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyī.
t.6.116.40: Then the prince, the delight of the Raghus, spoke sweetly to Bharata, the best of the righteous, in fitting and well-chosen words.
t.6.116.41: And my own excellent and spacious palace, with its aśoka grove, strewn with pearls and lapis lazuli, offer that to Sugrīva.
t.6.116.42: Having heard those words of his, Bharata, whose valour was true, took Sugrīva by the hand and entered that dwelling.
t.6.116.43: Then, urged on by Śatrughna, they quickly took oil lamps and coverings for the couches and entered.
t.6.116.44: And the greatly radiant younger brother of Rāghava said to Sugrīva: "O lord, command messengers for the consecration of Rāma."
t.6.116.45: Sugrīva swiftly gave to four chiefs of the monkeys four golden pitchers, adorned with all kinds of jewels.
t.6.116.46: O monkeys, act in such a way that at the hour of dawn you stand waiting with jars filled with the waters of the four oceans.
t.6.116.47: Thus addressed, the great-souled monkeys, resembling elephants, swiftly flew up into the sky like swift-moving Garuḍas.
t.6.116.49: Then Suṣeṇa, endowed with strength, brought from the eastern ocean a pitcher filled with water and adorned with all kinds of jewels.
t.6.116.48: Jāmbavān and Hanumān, the monkey Vegadarśī, and Ṛṣabha then brought pitchers filled with water. In jars they fetched the water of five hundred rivers.
t.6.116.50: Ṛṣabha swiftly brought water from the southern ocean.
t.6.116.51: Gavaya brought water from the great western ocean in a golden pitcher covered with red sandalwood and camphor.
t.6.116.53: Śatrughna, together with the ministers, informed the excellent family priest and the friends about the consecration of Rāma.
t.6.116.52: And from the northern ocean, he whose might was like the wind's, with the prowess of Garuḍa and the wind, swiftly brought cool water in a great jeweled pitcher.
t.6.116.54: Then the aged Vasiṣṭha, self-restrained and pure, together with the brāhmaṇas, seated Rāma along with Sītā upon a throne made of jewels.
t.6.116.55: Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, Jābāli and then Kāśyapa, Kātyāyana and Suyajña, Gautama and likewise Vijaya.
t.6.116.56: He consecrated that tiger among men with clear, fragrant water, just as the Vasus consecrated the thousand-eyed Vāsava.
t.6.116.57: Overjoyed, they had him consecrated, first by the officiating priests and brāhmaṇas, and then likewise by maidens, ministers and warriors, together with the merchants.
t.6.116.58: And also with the juices of all herbs, by the deities stationed in the sky, by the four guardians of the worlds, and by all the gods assembled together.
t.6.116.59: Śatrughna held over him a beautiful, pale-white parasol; Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, held a white yak-tail fan, and Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, held another, gleaming like the moon.
t.6.116.60: Urged by Vāsava, Vāyu gave to Rāghava a golden garland of a hundred lotuses, blazing with splendor.
t.6.116.61: Urged by Śakra, he gave to the lord of men a pearl necklace set with every kind of gem and adorned with jewels and precious stones.
t.6.116.62: Then, at the consecration of the wise Rāma, who was worthy of it, the celestial Gandharvas sang and the hosts of Apsarases danced.
t.6.116.63: At the festival of Rāghava, the earth became rich with crops, the trees laden with fruit, and the flowers fragrant.
t.6.116.64: Then that bull among men first gave to the twice-born a hundred thousand horses, milch cows and cattle, and a hundred bulls.
t.6.116.65: Rāghava further gave to the brāhmaṇas thirty crores of gold, along with costly ornaments and garments of many kinds.
t.6.116.66: The bull among men gave to Sugrīva a divine golden garland, resplendent like the rays of the sun and studded with gems.
t.6.116.67: And the steadfast one gave to Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, a pair of armlets studded with cat's-eye gems and adorned with diamonds and jewels.
t.6.116.68: And Rāma gave to Sītā an unsurpassed necklace of pearls, adorned with the finest gems and shining with a radiance like the rays of the moon.
t.6.116.69: Glancing toward her lord, Vaidehī gave to the son of Vāyu a pair of spotless celestial garments and splendid ornaments.
t.6.116.70: Taking off the necklace from her own neck, the daughter of Janaka looked again and again at all the monkeys and at her husband.
t.6.116.71: Seeing her, he who understood her gestures said to the daughter of Janaka: "O fortunate one, give the necklace, O beautiful lady, to him with whom you are pleased."
t.6.116.72: The dark-eyed lady gave that necklace to the son of Vāyu, in whom manliness, valour and wisdom ever abide.
t.6.116.73: Hanūmān, the bull among monkeys, shone with that necklace, white as a mass of moonbeams, like a mountain with a white cloud.
t.6.116.74: Then the lord of the earth, the scorcher of foes, having looked to it, bestowed upon Dvivida and Mainda, and upon Nīla, all the objects of their desire.
t.6.116.75: All the elders among the monkeys, and the other lords of the monkeys as well, were duly honored with garments and ornaments, each according to his merit.
t.6.116.76: All of them, duly honoured as each deserved with abundant gifts of whatever they desired and with jewels, went back, all with joyful hearts, the way they had come.
t.6.116.77: The supremely noble Rāghava gave his commands with the greatest joy, and Rāma, devoted to dharma, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, the knower of dharma.
t.6.116.78: O knower of dharma, together with me govern this earth, which the kings of old held by their strength; equal to me, take up in the office of heir-apparent that burden which was borne by our forefathers.
t.6.116.79: When Saumitri, though entreated with all earnestness and being appointed to the office of heir-apparent on earth, would not consent, the great-souled one then consecrated Bharata.
t.6.116.80: And Rāghava, righteous of soul, having attained the unsurpassed kingdom, performed sacrifices of many kinds together with his friends, brothers and kinsmen.
t.6.116.81: That bull among kings performed sacrifices again and again: the Pauṇḍarīka and the Aśvamedha, the Vājapeya, and many other kinds of sacrifice.
t.6.116.82: Having obtained the kingdom, Rāghava, for ten thousand years, performed a hundred horse sacrifices, with excellent horses and abundant sacrificial fees.
t.6.116.83: Long-armed, his arms reaching to his knees, broad-shouldered and majestic, Rāma, with Lakṣmaṇa as his companion, protected and ruled the earth.
t.6.116.84: While Rāma ruled the kingdom, widows did not lament, there was no fear caused by beasts of prey, nor any fear born of disease.
t.6.116.85: The world became free of robbers, and no misfortune touched anyone; nor did the elders ever perform the funeral rites for the young.
t.6.116.86: Everything was joyful indeed, and everyone was devoted to dharma. Looking to Rāma alone, they did not harm one another.
t.6.116.88: The trees, their branches spread wide, were ever in flower and ever in fruit; the rain-cloud poured its rain in due season, and the wind was pleasant to the touch.
t.6.116.87: While Rāma ruled the kingdom, for thousands of years the people, each the father of thousands of sons, lived free from disease and free from sorrow.
t.6.116.89: While Rāma ruled, the people engaged in their own duties, content with their own work alone; they were devoted to dharma and were never false.
t.6.116.90: All were endowed with auspicious marks, all were devoted to dharma; for ten thousand years Rāma ruled the kingdom.
